text: Colossian is a stone golem located at Brimstone Garrison in Zaralek Cavern.
Corrupt Force of Nature are corrupted treants in the service of Celebras the Cursed in Maraudon.
Corrupting Shadows is a void revenant that corrupted Archmage Xylem. The shadows are defeated and Xylem rescued.
Flaming was an enchantment that caused flames to sheathe a weapon.
Council Icecallers are draenei located in the Vault of the Incarnates.

Crevan Falamar was a human mage. He had alligned himself with Malygos during the Nexus War, and was therefore placed inside the Violet Hold by the Kirin Tor. The Kirin Tor told Crevan's family that he had died in battle. Later he tricked his nephew, Aodhan, to open his cell and locate a book inside Dalaran's library, a book that could return the powers, that the Kirin Tor has removed, back to him. He later used the book to open the other cells of the Violet Hold. Finally he attempted to make Dalaran drop from the sky, but he was stopped by Aodhan, Rhonin and Simeon.
Crushfist is a mo'arg brute located in Val'sharah during the Legion Assaults.
Flails, also known as horseman's flails or sometimes morningstars or mace-on-a-sticks, were a type of one-handed, martial melee weapon.
Crysta Flutterwing is a faerie flight master located in Dreamsong Fenn in Ardenweald.
Cyclothar is an air elemental being tamed by Wind Tamer Kagan and his two fellow Wind Tamers at Camp Winterhoof in the Howling Fjord.
Cursed Jades are unbound earth elementals located in the Greenstone Village scenario.
Flame blade was an evocation spell that created a sword-like beam of fire that extended from the caster's hand and performed similar to a scimitar.
__NOTOC__ Cyclarus is an air elemental located in the Eye of the Vortex in Darkshore.
Dark Chronicler is a troll spectre located in the Throat of Xibala in Zuldazar. It is the last remnant of the worshippers of Xibala.
Dark Rune Commoners are iron dwarves located, as part of the Thorim encounter, in Ulduar.
Captain Flinn was a sailor on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR.

__NOTOC__ Dazar was the founder and first king of Zandalar. He led an exodus of his people out of the muck and mire, united the tribes, and built a city of gold. He was an undefeated warrior and the first tamer of raptors. Recently, King Dazar alongside his raptor companions Reban and T'zala was resurrected by the Prophet Zul and his forces using techniques learned from the revival of Lei Shen, to lead Zul's dreamed empire in Rastakhan's place.
__NOTOC__ Death-Caller Majuli is an ice troll located in Island Expedition.
Death Singers are banshees that roam around the Noxious Glade in the Eastern Plaguelands.

Flame shield was a divine magic spell available to druids of Eldath, the Goddess of Singing Waters. It created an intangible barrier attached to the caster's hand that extinguished normal and magical fires. The shield could be passed to others.

__NOTOC__ Deathfang is Margrave Draka's pet helhound. He is a fierce hunter and faithful friend who enjoys playing fetch. Deathfang helps defend the Bleak Redoubt when it's attacked by Baron Vyraz's forces, fighting alongside the Soulfused Construct. He can be seen sleeping in the Covenant Sanctum version of the Seat of the Primus, in the northeastern corner of the main hall. The hound accompanies Draka to Stonevigil Overlook in Revendreth on the mission to stop the Tithelord. When Provisoner Kraus escapes the town with an anima shipment, Draka and the heroes mount Deathfang to catch up with and stop the carriage. Later, Deathfang participates in the assault on the House of Rituals, fighting at the southern entrance to the house. During the world quest Deathfang's Favorite Toy, the hound can be found southeast of the Theater of Pain and players have to help him exercise using a Throwin' Skull.
Decaying Colossus is a flesh giant found at the top of the stairs inside the Plagueworks of Icecrown Citadel.
Deckard is a level 100 felhound found alongside its master Dru Dobbs in Dreadscar Rift.
The Flashing Blade at Dusk Troupe was a group of "bravos" (blademasters) led by Davien Mecatoris, that operated out of Sambral, one of the Windrise Ports of Laerakond as of 1479 DR.

__NOTOC__ Derek the Undying is a Forsaken mage trainer in the War Quarter of Undercity, which seems to be an unusual place for a mage trainer. Derek conducted an arcane ritual in the Dalaran Crater, at the convergence of multiple powerful ley lines. Alliance forces were sent to put an end to his ritual.
Dinorae Swiftfeather is a night elf flight master located at the Shrine of Aviana in the Mount Hyjal.

]] ]] Dire bears are gigantic bears, perhaps 20 feet tall when they rear onto their hind legs. They can grow between 12 feet ans 18-20 feet. They can weigh between 6,000-8,000 pounds. They have a rich dark coat of fur in shades between brown and black, and a powerful build. Some have been spotted in Mulgore and Ashenvale. They avoid humans but show no fear if provoked. Occasionally, a dire bear will eat livestock or even attack lone travelers for food, but such action is rare. They are good swimmers and may attack from the water; others hunt seals. A dire bear will attempt to get a good hold on a victim and then bite until the victim is dead. Some dire bears are known to have bony protrusions all over their body, as if their skeletons were trying to fight their way out. The omnivorous dire bear usually does not bother creatures that assiduously try to avoid it, but it aggressively defends a kill or other source of food. It does not hesitate to rip apart anything that might contain something edible. Beastmasters, such as Tagar Bearclaw, keep a dire bear as a companion.
A flame tongue was a rare type of magical sword with a burning blade.
Direflame is an unbound elemental battle pet located at The Felblight in Tanaan Jungle.
Direflame Elemental is a fire elemental summoned by Urda Direflame in Zuldazar.
Disquieted Frost are ice elementals located at Gelikyr Overlook in Thaldraszus.
Flaming burst was a weapon enchantment that caused flames to sheathe a weapon and explode against a target.

The doomguard or doom guard (sometimes pluralized as doomguards or doom guards) are a type of demonic warrior of the ered'ruin species that used to work as Archimonde's personal escort, and serve the Burning Legion with great fervor. Powerful and deliberate, these winged aberrations are known across the cosmos for their brutality. The doomguard are utterly devoted to their pit lord masters and revel in the destruction of worlds. They serve as commanders of the Legion front-line forces, and are versatile in the use of fire magic and dark curses, as well as melee attacks.

Drann was a half-orc that had teamed up with Captain Dumont, Stonehoof, a tauren, Feulia, a half-Kaldorei archer, Makil, a goblin tinker, and two siblings, Renmar and Talario who were human mages. The companions had stolen a magic jar from a centaur camp in the Barrens after hearing of a legend. According to the legend, the jar would unlock untold riches in an ancient shrine nearby. They fought their way through centaur and quilboars to the shrine. Dumont had lost his life in the process. Drann impatiently asked if the jar was intact after the fight, "his father's impatient orc blood getting the better of his mother's calming human influence". The jar was in good condition. They found an ancient Darnassian dialect carved on the shrine that was the same one carved onto the jar. A warning was placed on the shrine stating, "...sealing them away so that our world might know new life." He helped clear away the corpses and the rubble discovering an altar underneath. After the brother and sister mages had completed a ritual, Drann shattered the jar with his fist. They had accidentally unleashed a towering fire elemental who promised to take them to his home in the Elemental Plane where they would be "rewarded". The elemental then began to rip a hole in the fabric of the universe. The landscape of the Barrens was pulled away to reveal the Firelands. Makil, believing that this wasn't any reward that they would want, asked Drann if they could all go home.

Dralad was an adventurous orange proto-dragon. He was the brother of Alexstrasza and Ysera, and the three of them were the only survivors of their clutch. His dead body was discovered by Alexstrasza and Malygos after he'd gone missing on a hunt. It was later revealed he was a victim of the rampaging Galakrond. His body went missing later on, presumably having become one of the not-living like Galakrond's other victims.
Flame dagger was an evocation spell that created a dagger-like blade of pure flame to appear in the hand of the caster.
Drained Emerald Drakes are green drakes found throughout the Emerald Dreamway. While they were sleeping, they were attacked by Void Haunts, who filled them with Void dreams. They may never wake up.
Dread Captain Winge was the captain of The Casket Carrier, which brought Horde players to battle in the Strand of the Ancients. He couldn't be killed.
__NOTOC__ Dreadflame Corruptors are eredar located in Farondale in Azsuna and Stormheim during the Legion Assaults.
A flensing gauntlet was a special type of magical spiked gauntlet.
Drathax, the Twilight Caller was a twilight dragonspawn located in Silithus.

Dreadtalon is a condor found in the Dragon Wastes of Dragonblight. He has been attacking numerous Horde caravans traveling to and from Venomspite, and for this Captain Gort has orders from Overlord Agmar to tell players to kill him.
Drek the Firecaller is a Burning Blade orc that attacks the garrison in order to retrieve the Heart of Gorgorek.
Firestaff was a rare evocation spell that added magical flame to a wooden melee weapon.
Dresaron is a dragon located at the Tainted Burrow, in Darkheart Thicket.
Dreamguard Erezsra is a wylderdrake located in the Ohn'ahran Plains.
Dreamguard Felyasra is a wylderdrake located in the Ohn'ahran Plains.
Flame's Forge was a significantly oversized enchanted tower shield that originated from a lost tomb in Anauroch.

Branimern Rythil was a Red Wizard conjurer and Nar demonbinder that sought out the unholy secrets of the ancient Narfell empire during the late 14 century DR. After transforming herself into a cambion, she went on to establish a stronghold in the ruins of Jastaath Castle on Mount Nar in the 15 century DR.
Capnolithyl, also known as Brimstone, was a vampiric smoke drake and a hero of the last Rage of Dragons.
Cerebriliths were tanar'ri demons of incredible physical strength and dangerous mental acuity. The Abyssal natives possessed potent psionic powers in addition to their fearsome fiendish ones.
The Flame Sword of Lolth, sometimes simply referred to as the Flame Sword, was a powerful artifact that served Lolth during the War of the Seldarine.
Chanelle Hallwinter was a knight of the famed Hallwinter family who, after her passing, returned as a restless ghost beneath the city of Neverwinter.
Daricon Beranos was a restless wraith that lingered in Myth Drannor during the late 14 century DR.

Duc-Sum Li was a Shou knight and healer who was the Regent of the Xiousing District in Marsember. He was a descendent of Emperor Li of the Shou Dynasty of Might. He was still active in his extreme old age in 1479 DR, exercising and meditating daily.
The First Light was a legendary holy undead bane longsword among the faithful of Lathander. The sword belonged to Commander Lyssic of Myth Drannor before the Weeping War destroyed the City of Song.

The fey eladrin were the most powerful of the eladrin, a subrace of elves who adopted the Feywild as their home. After centuries of exposure to that plane's magic, they acquired supernatural abilities not seen on most of their kin from the Prime Material plane and were effectively transformed into fey. Sometimes called noble eladrin, they were capable of changing their physical appearance and powers according to their mood, assuming characteristics of the seasons.

Arondil, formerly of Dawnstar, is an Altmeri Necromancer and Ice Mage experimenting with necroanimus. After being "evicted" from Dawnstar for his experiments, Arondil took refuge in the icy depths of Yngvild where he endeavors to "reanimate and enslave the dead." Arondil has an obsession with the young milkmaids of Dawnstar and has found a way to bolster his already unique entirely female draugr entourage with their reanimated specters, the Yngvild Ghosts.

Atronach Workers are peaceful Flame and Air Atronachs summoned by Eldellar on the island of Artaeum. A Storm Atronach Worker can be found further east where it produces small rain clouds to water the plants. Mulvarion is watching it tend to the fields nearby.
Fish oil was the natural oils extracted from the bodies of various fatty fish. It was used in alchemy, ship-building, tool crafting, and as a spell component.
A Frost Atronach makes up in strength what it lacks in speed. Its freezing grip can do lasting frost damage, and it can hurl icy chunks of its body great distances.
Halldir is a spectral draugr mage encountered in Halldir's Cairn and serves as the final boss in this dungeon.
Ice Wraiths are swift, elemental creatures of ice and snow in . They move quickly and use powerful frost attacks.
Fireguard Fortress was an ancient dwarfhold that was built into the side of Mount Hotenow on the Sword Coast North.

The Imperial Simulacrum is the official term for the events that took place when Jagar Tharn took the Imperial crown from Emperor Uriel Septim VII. Jagar Tharn was a mage-priest at the Temple of Sethiete in Camlorn, High Rock before his ascension to the position of Imperial Battlemage. In 3E 376, after sleeping with her, he tricked Queen Barenziah of Mournhold to show him the way to Old Mournhold, where the Staff of Chaos was hidden. He then stole the staff and disappeared. Later, he managed to become the Imperial Battlemage of Uriel Septim VII. In 3E 389, he captured Uriel VII and banished him into Oblivion with the Staff of Chaos. Normally when the Emperor of Tamriel dies, the Elder Council is magically informed by the Amulet of Kings and meets to select a successor. By sequestering Uriel Septim VII in another dimension, where time ran slower, Tharn prevented this from happening. He then broke the staff into eight pieces and hid them in the other provinces of Tamriel. Using his powerful, and skillful knack for Illusion, he took on the visage of Uriel VII, and ruled the Empire, replacing the Emperor's guard and servants with Daedra. Several years later, he made a bargain with Daedric Prince Mehrunes Dagon to invade Battlespire, the Imperial training facility and bastion of the Imperial Battlemages. This move was essential to secure his position and to eliminate a possible threat to his reign. Mehrunes Dagon was destroyed and cast back into Oblivion by a mysterious hero, but

The Knight is the most noble of all combatants. Knights are strong in body and in character, are well schooled in the art of chivalry, and conduct themselves with honor and dignity. Knights are adept at the utilization of all weapons, can wear many types of armor, and typically utilize shields. Knights are also adept at armor and weapons repair, and in some instances have an immunity to paralysis primarily due to their strong moral character.

Stenwick Gurles is a Breton and the current Sentinel of the Viridian Woods. One day, he stumbled upon the unconscious and injured Princess Elara, Queen Arzhela's daughter. He brought her back to his cabin in the woods, where he tended to her wounds and nursed her back to health with the help of special powers granted to him by his title. In doing so, he unintentionally groomed her to be his successor, as he is growing quite old.
Flintknapping was a skill and craft used by the Azuposi people of the Pasocada Basin of Maztica.

Volkihar Master Vampires are the highest level Vampires encountered in . Like with all Vampires, the Dragonborn can contract Sanguinare Vampiris from their attacks. They are extremely deadly, casting Destruction spells and Vampiric Drain, which can sap large amounts of health. They generally use Ice Spike when encountered at higher levels, and Frostbite at lower levels. They are usually accompanied by one or two Volkihar Vampires, as Volkihar Master Vampires are leaders of the Volkihar Clan.

The Baknamy are a humanoid race in Final Fantasy XII and Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift. They are easily identified by their small stature, green skin, and horns that protrude from their heads. One defining feature are the specialized gas masks they must wear at all times to filter out unbreathable air. Baknamy act in part as the goblins of early-era Ivalice, though goblins also exist within the setting. While the Baknamy do not entirely resemble the traditional goblin, they are short and squat as goblins usually are, and use a variant of the Goblin Punch. They are also surprisingly powerful for their size, and capable of using magic quite proficiently in spite of their low intelligence.

Crescent Unit Phantasma is an enemy from Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII-. He can dish out a lot of physical damage with Chain Thrust and magic damage with Firaga. He can inflict instant death with Death Missile. Aside from equipping protection for Instant Death, Crescent Unit Phantasma can be fought in a similar manner as all other Crescent Units.
Flank of the Virgin was a unique enchanted shield made out of the hull of a small Reghedmen boat in the late 13 century DR.

The Hellgaroo Mage is an enemy from Final Fantasy III. It is found on the plains of the Surface World and in the Dragon Spire in southeastern Saronia. They are fond of casting Break, Fira and Blizzara.

The Marionette is an enemy from Final Fantasy IV. They often appear in large groups alongside a single Marionetteer, which should be eliminated first before attention is turned to these puppets. Marionettes have access to a wide variety of spells, including Fire, Thunder, Blizzard and Berserk, but are not particularly threatening.

Noel is one of two playable characters in Final Fantasy XIII-2 and can be used as party leader. If the two main player characters, Serah and Noel, become knocked out, it is Game Over. Noel prioritizes agility and strength and fights with dual swords. When used as the party leader, the player controls Noel in battle and on the field. The party leader can be changed on-the-fly, but there are segments where Noel is not in the party. There is a boss battle that the player must do as just Noel, however. On the field, the main character can jump and use Mog's abilities. He can summon and command monsters via the Paradigm Pack system. His victory pose is to put his two swords back together into one and swing it onto his back.
Fizban's platinum shield was a spell used by sorcerers, and wizards to protect themselves and others.

SOLDIER Trooper is an enemy in Chapters 5, 9, and 10 of Dirge of Cerberus -Final Fantasy VII-. He is dressed like a traditional SOLDIER of Shinra, and fights like one, using a sword rather than a gun. He is very fast and powerful, but has no ranged attacks, so can be defeated at a distance. His weak point is his head.
Kern "The Hammer" is a half-orc and a multiclassed barbarian/monk. Kern fights in a Vasselheim arena called the Crucible. As an NPC, he is portrayed by Matthew Mercer.
(pronounced TIE-sha /[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English `taɪʃə]/) is an orc druid of the Circle of Ancients played by Aabria Iyengar in Campaign Four.
Fists of the Legion were enchanted maces created to be used against orcs who once menaced the Sword Coast.

A spirit resided in the wreck of a smuggler's ship on the Barren Shores of Wildemount. It is tethered via a curse to a golden chair in the ship's hull. This spirit animated items and cargo aboard the ship, including swords, rugs, and armor to slaughter the original crew.
The Titan is a Guardian class which specializes in armor. The first Titans built and defended The Wall that protects The City. Their heritage is rooted in strength, sacrifice, and mercilessness.

The Aspirants of Nezarec are Ultra-class Shadow Legion soldiers devoted to Nezarec, seen aboard Essence. Encountered in the Root of Nightmares Raid, these heavy hitting and extremely durable enemies are seen within the varying transitions between the Raid's encounters, where they attempt to prevent the Guardians from reaching Nezarec.
Flaylan was a cowardly spear-wielding orc who served red dragon Firkraag in his maze in the Windspear Hills of Amn in the late 14 century DR.
Lucent Arc Hoarders are a type of Lightbearer Wizard encountered within Savathûn's Spire. They can be distinguished by the blue glow of the Arc Light they are infused with.

The Lord Sayter (Goat Lord) is an cut boss enemy. He was likely tied to some Quest on Level 7. He would be powerful winged Goatman with a scythe. He was repurposed to make Satyr Lord in Hellfire. He works in the game and uses Skeleton AI. There were also two Unique Goat Lords, which is weird because the base monster is already an boss, Blighstone is set to a color palette which changes all yellow colors on his body to red, he was also instead an Unique of Invisible Lord in pre-release. Soulslasher The Hollow exists only in Pre-release.
Sir Tomas the Gyrfalcon was a knight heralded for his bravery and speed. He took the gyrfalcon as his coat of arms, soaring to victory many times beneath its wings.
Flame Quencher was a unique axe forged by the song-smith named Gehorg Diamondforge of Ravens Bluff in the late 14 century DR.

Fluffymon is a Mini Bird Digimon. It goes about its activities while hiding within the luxuriant leaves of the forest trees. Its wings are undeveloped so it cannot yet fly, but it is agile enough to scamper up even vertical tree trunks. When Fluffymon deems that the threat has been sufficiently intimidated, it flees as fast as it possibly can. Attacks *Birdy Head: Utilizes its speed to attack with a headbutt.

Gizamon is a Sea Animal Digimon. It grew fins on its hands and feet in order to paddle through water. It is more suited for life in the water than on land, and although it swims about quickly in the water with its fins and strong hind-legs, on the ground, it moves about with weak, frog-like hops. When on land, it has a very timid disposition, but when in the water, it displays its natural, ferocious personality. Attacks *Spiral Saw (Spiral Edge): Rolls up into a ball and uses its blade-like fins to attack an opponent. *Frog Kick *Water Cure: Fires a stream of water at the enemy. *Water Shot: Attacks with a bursting stream of water.

Kakamon is a Beast Digimon. It is clad in beautiful red and gold fur. Kakamon takes special care of its trademark, mohawk-like hair atop its head. It can been found in various habitats throughout vast regions of Shambala. Kakamon has an upbeat nature, enjoying singing and music, and will proudly make other Digimon it encounters listen to its songs. There are many Kakamon that yearn for the lifestyle of a lone wolf such as the popular Pandamon, as shown by the Pandamon sticker on their headphones. Attacks *: Curls its body up like a ball and smashes into its opponent. *: Unleashes a powerful sonic attack using its voice, which has been trained through song.
Fleshrender, once known as Barney, was an enchanted short sword that could temporarily negate the target's healing.

Lee Jianliang is one of the main protagonists of Digimon Tamers. He is the partner of Terriermon, as well as Lee Shaochung's elder brother. =Profile= Jianliang is half-Chinese and half-Japanese: his father (Jiang-yu) is Chinese and his mother (Mayumi) is Japanese. He is the third oldest of four siblings: he has a 17-year-old brother, Rinchei, and a 15-year-old sister, Jaarin, as well as a 7-year-old sister, Shaochung. Along with his father, Jianliang is a Tai-chi student, studying art under a Sensei who is a family friend. In a moment of self-reflection, Jianliang confessed that he had been an extremely willful child and that having three siblings forced him to become self-reliant and independent. His study of martial arts was also revealed to be a way of asserting himself to stand out amongst his large family. Once, he got into a serious argument with a neighborhood child and, presumably in a moment of thoughtlessness, injured the child with his Tai-chi skills. Since realizing the error of his ways, Jianliang devoted himself to practicing self-restraint, fearing that he might hurt someone else if he were to lose control of his emotions again. He became responsible, quiet, and a soft-spoken person who conducts himself with maturity, but also tends to blame himself for things beyond his control. When he was first introduced, he was practical and knowledgeable. Being reserved resulted in clashes with the seemingly cold and indifferent Ruki. However, he was willing to help Takat

.]]Parias the Cleric is one of the three playable hero classes in Hexen. He appears as a well-armored man in chain mail with a horned helmet, cape, and leather gloves and boots. An ornate black tunic with red accents is worn around his waist. Parias has the most even balance of speed, armor, magic, and strength among the three classes, second in strength only to Baratus and in magic only to Daedolon. A stalwart soldier of the Church, but also skilled in the arcane, Parias is the most well-rounded class in the game. The cleric is probably the easiest class in the game to play as, possessing both enough physical endurance to survive most attacks and a powerful magical arsenal for dealing with ranged combat. He is an effective class throughout much of the game as much of his general playstyle is similar to that of most first person shooters, a melee weapon as a last resort and ranged weapons requires that require ammunition (in the form of mana). The primary drawback of the cleric is that his first tier weapon is fairly slow and less effective than the other first tier weapons: although it has marginally longer reach than the Baratus' gauntlets, and slightly greater damage than the Daedolon's staff, it is overall significantly weaker and shorter ranged than each of those. This means that that players seeking to output enough damage to quickly defeat their opponents will find themselves very dependent on mana. Wildcat is a character in Fortnite: Save the World that represents the Soldier class. Her model is used in the following subclasses: *Centurion: Uses and to dramatically boost the damage of the squad. *Demolisher: Specializes in fighting crowds of enemies with explosive shells and grenades that regenerate more quickly in combat. First Blood was a bastard sword found in Wheloon Prison in the mid-1480s DR.

Jason Carthalion, of the renowned Carthalion lineage, was a mighty hero from the Ice Age of Dominaria. He was a ward to Oriel Kjeldos, the champion of Clan Emerald of Storgard and a user of green mana.

Deep Winter was the AI assigned to the survey team on planet Onyx, Zone 67. He took the form of an old man with a snowy cape that blew snowflakes and ice as it "moved." Though it is never specifically mentioned, Deep Winter seems to have replaced Eternal Spring when the "smart" AI "died" in 2537. Deep Winter was a 5th generation "smart" AI, which may possess longer life spans than previous generations of UNSC AI, or a "dumb AI," as it seems he lived from 2537 until 2551, double the number of years a 3rd generation smart AI lives. Deep Winter was known to be very talkative. He seemed to enjoy the company of Kurt-051, SCPO Franklin Mendez, and the SPARTAN-IIIs at Camp Currahee. Deep Winter also showed great concern for the young Spartans and often acted in what he thought to be their best interest, even when not ordered to do so. He monitored the progress and actions of the Beta Company Spartans even after they graduated, and then monitored the progress of the Gamma Company Spartans as well. In 2551, he discovered the illegal drugs used in the augmentation process of the Gammas and tried to warn Kurt-051 via a secret Slipspace COM launcher. He was shut down soon after, as he had reached the end of his operational lifespan, but left files for Kurt to trace the source of the drugs. Ironically, Kurt was the one who was responsible for the illegal drugs, and he promptly had the files erased. They both thought they had done what was best for the Spartan-IIIs. Deep Winter was replace

Antonio Agama is a world famous Avaloran explorer who appears in the Elena of Avalor episode "The Gecko's Tale". Always getting himself into trouble, he was turned into a giant gecko after stealing a treasure known as the Golden Gecko, so Princess Elena, Princess Isabel, and Gabe help him return it so he can return to normal.
Flame enamelled armor was a set of enchanted half-plate armor used by the Flaming Fists mercenary company of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR.

Flower Mario is the form Mario takes upon collecting a Super Flower Pot in Super Mario Bros. Wonder – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Meetup in Bellabel Park. Flower Mario wears a red tulip costume, and can create flower projectiles that rise up through ceilings and can defeat enemies, destroy jars, and trigger Wow Buds. Spin Jumps create two flowers on both sides. Flowers created from Spin Jumping move slighty slower than flowers created by pressing . Flower Mario can also perform a Flower jump, a jump in which he flutters his leaves to extend his jump (similar to Yoshi's Flutter Jump) and then slowly floats downward in a manner similar to other flight-based power-ups. Like Elephant Mario, Flower Mario can even store water in his petals and spray them one at a time when Spin Jumping, performing a midair spin, or performing a Flower jump. Three weeks prior to Super Mario Bros. Wonder – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Meetup in Bellabel Parks release, Flower Mario debuted in Super Mario Run as a statue, in an event promoting the game running from March 5, 2026, to April 3, 2026. The statue can be obtained by completing the first stamp card.

Orco (known as Shachee in Japanese and in the European English GameCube version) is a large blue and a Jungle Buddy in Donkey Kong Jungle Beat. He appears in only one level, Pristine Sea, where he is generally found simply wandering around aimlessly. Donkey Kong can approach Orco and grab on to his dorsal fin to ride him. Like Enguarde, Orco can smash through underwater barriers. He can also leap out of the water and reach heights. The New Play Control! version specifically refers to Orco as "he", officially identifying him as male. Despite this, Orco has several traits that are more commonly associated with real-world female killer whales. Most notably, Orco's dorsal fin resembles the shorter, more curved one of a female killer whale as opposed to the longer, triangular dorsal fin of a male killer whale. Additionally, several smaller killer whales follow behind Orco, which is a trait shared with real world dolphins. This is a similar case to an aquatic Animal Friend, Glimmer, who is referred to as male despite resembling a female anglerfish.

Kisame jumps into the air and then points Samehada down towards the opponent and then enveloping it in water. He then manipulates its shape moulding it into a shark and drilling the opponent into the ground. es:Caída de Tiburón Hambriento
Flameheart, favored weapon of Gwaeron Windstrom, was a +1 flaming giant bane greatsword.

Luax is the last droid sent by Esmeraude to capture Chibiusa for Prince Demande. She has a very elegant humanoid appearance and lives inside another dimension called the Cosmic Time Warp; a bleak, empty void in time. She appears to be the only living creature that dwells there. She appeared in episode 82 of Sailor Moon R. She can alter time to send her opponents' attacks back at them. She can also extend her finger nails into claws and use her hair as a weapon. After scattering the Sailor Guardians, Tuxedo Mask, Luna, Artemis, and Chibiusa across the Time Warp, Esmeraude sent Luax to capture Chibiusa (deliberately forgetting to tell her to capture Sailor Moon, whom Demande has fallen in love with and ordered Esmeraude to bring to him). Luax disguised herself as Chibiusa's mother in an attempt to trick her but wasn't able to fool Chibiusa. Chibiusa fought Luax with a slingshot but was unable to damage her. The Sailor Guardians appeared and attacked her but their attacks were sent back at them. Sailor Mercury discovered that the flow of time is back to normal for a moment after the droid attacks. Chibiusa attacked the Luax, distracting her, and the Sailor Guardians combined their powers to blast five colorcoded energy beams (Sailor Planet Attack) at the Luax, killing her.

Elite guards are a special cadre of female ghosts employed by the Terran Confederacy remnants. They are tougher than the typical ghost. Several were used to guard a science facility that was raided by the Kimeran Pirates.

Rodimus Prime is more than just a high ranking Autobot officer, and he doesn't need a badge to prove it! He is extremely popular amongst some of his fellow Autobot brethren, and has mastered several different combat skills, such as servo-to-servo combat. While he has mastered the use of various defensive weaponry, his personal weapon of choice is his uniquely-designed energy bow. Rodimus is a born leader and strives to become the next Magnus. In battle, He looks out for everyone, including the enemy, thus making him a great ally in battle. War is not a game to him, though outside of battle, he is really a nice guy.

Flying was a quality that could be applied to melee weapons. The weapon could be commanded to follow very simple orders, though it was not intelligent, and it could fly like an animated object. Flying weapons could also be used to guard a location, just like an animated skeleton could.

:Wire Tap V20 is a Decepticon Real Gear Robot from the live-action movie continuity family. Wire Tap V20 is a jerk. Pure and simple. He's a master codebreaker, capable of hacking wireless carrier signals. He could be moving billions of dollars in currency around the world market, hacking nuclear command satellites, and causing panic and misinformation on a planetary scale. Instead, he uses his powers to make it look like you sent embarrassing emails and then puts porn in your browser history at work. Watch out: He's got a camera built into his face, and you can just bet your private "happy time" is going on YouTube. : French-Canadian name: Decodeur V20 : Spanish name: Descodificador V20

Tarset (Hand of Antu-Herap) is an Arisen. Among the Sesha-Hebsu, Tarset is something of an oddity. She does not have a contemplative soul, or an instinct for scholarship. Tarset is observant, and persistent, in her own way, and she is very, very good at it. Once she has set her mind on something, there is very little that can stop her from achieving her goal. Excelling at snap judgments, and with martial talents that few in her guild process, she is a force to be reckoned with. Currently, she serves Antu-Herap, her good friend (in her mind, at least), and rescuer. Tarset is missing large chunks of her existence, but Antu-Herap has told her that during her forgotten time, she made a mistake. Luckily, he was there to help her fix it, and the first thing she could do in penance is to forget what she did. Antu-Herap is the one who trained a cult to support her, and he is the one who sends her on some of her quests. Tarset believes that a person should run, not walk, through life. It's possible that she's running from a darkness now forgotten, but it doesn't matter. She's here to serve her guild, and continue the hunt. She always has the hunt.
Ahunite Frostwinds are air elementals summoned by Lord Ahune.

The Forest of Tethir, also known as Wealdath, was the largest forest in the Lands of Intrigue and on the Sword Coast and one of the largest in all of Faerûn. Some scholars were of the opinion that the forest was the "single most important thing" that set the culture of Tethyr.

The Crystal People are beings who reside in the Crystal Dimension and, for a short while, held Quartzion as their ruler. They are rock-hard, making them difficult to fight. The only time they have been shown being defeated is when Quartzion kills a group of them with a laser from her trunk.

Doctor Prince, Doctor Princess' gender-swapped version, plays a small role in "Bad Little Boy." In Ice King's story, he steals the Enchiridion from Fionna and Cake. Gunter fires its laser canon at him, but he claims that lasers cannot hurt him because he is a "really strong guy" and took his "doctor pills" that morning. He then throws a dolphin at Fionna and Cake but misses. Then he hoots like a monkey and throws what appears to be the Enchiridion to Fionna. It turns out to be a time bomb, which Fionna tosses just before it explodes in a shower of confetti. Ice King then comes out of a portal in the Enchiridion and reprimands him. Doctor Prince, ashamed, admits that Ice King is correct and sees "his side of things." He then jetpacks away with the flip of a switch on his monogrammed belt buckle.

The Goo Skulls are a species of skeleton that reside in the Vault of Bones. They are seen crawling on walls and can eject streams of adhesive "goo" originating from an organ in the rib cage from their mouths. They use this stream to both catch and encase their prey like spiders. They live in cave systems made out of this same goo.

The Flying Blade was one of the artifacts of The Nine. The spirit of Relve Langral was bound to the sword and could be called forth by the sword's owner and would unquestionably follow the owner's commands. His mind was twisted by Myrkul and he enjoyed killing. Relve's spirit was wreathed in blue flames when he was outside of the sword, which is why Relve is referred to as a blueflame ghost. The sword had been in the possession of the Stormserpent family of Suzail for many years. Elminster sought the sword and the other relics to feed to Alassra Silverhand to restore her sanity.

Maja the Sky Witch is a character who first appears in "Sky Witch." She bought Hambo from Ash and later trades Hambo to Princess Bubblegum in exchange for the latter's rock t-shirt. She uses the shirt's emotional essence for a brew, which she says will be "something big." Her companion is the Crabbit Familiar, whom she abuses. She has the ability to hover and can shoot bolts of electricity from her hands. Maja is accidentally put in a coma by the Ancient Psychic Tandem War Elephant after trying to conquer the Candy Kingdom with Darren the Ancient Sleeper in "Something Big ." Later, the Ancient Psychic Tandem War Elephant, wishing to be more than a war machine, retrieves the comatose Maja and psychically explains that it will care for her and keep her alive, much to her irritation. She remains in a coma until "Come Along With Me ," where Betty Grof and King Man use her to try to seize control of GOLB's dark energies. Maja finally wakes up when Betty's irritation with Ice King causes an emotional surge, but the energies overwhelm her and she explodes a few seconds later. In "Together Again," she is seen in the 1st dead world, where the worst of the worst go. However, she ascends to a better place; it is unknown if she really redeemed herself.
Muscle Prince plays a small role "Bad Little Boy." He appears at Lumpy Space Prince's party, dancing with Female Wormo. He is the male counterpart of Muscle Princess, created by Marceline.

The Shadow Horse (or Shadow Steed), so far, makes its first and only appearance in "Wizard." Finn created it from his shadow using shadowcery. He then attempted to ride on it, but he passed right through the horse. Shadow Horse dissolves shortly after saying "No touchies!" He makes sounds like a normal horse and speaks English. The shadow steed in also he seems to be in one Adventure Time commercial saying his quote. He also seems to have a similar physical appearance to Lord Monochromicorn.
Force was a magical quality that could be added to any weapon, even ammunition such as arrows.

The Netherese Archwizard Quantoul is born, creator of dozens of spells and founder of the city of Jockteleg. * Netherese arcanists hunt down the forces of the ogre mage Storm. After a battle north of the Southfill River, the ogres are defeated. It is unknown if Storm himself is killed, though his people never bother the Netherese again.
* Lady Decampus — the "Singing Lady" — is killed in a spell-battle by archwizard Delzjhava on the frontier of Netheril.
* In this productive year, Netherese arcanist Trebbe develops both antimagic shell and minor globe of invulnerability in his research of protective magic.
Fort Locke was a garrison located at the southern end of the Mere of Dead Men along the Sword Coast.
*Netherese arcanist Smolyn invents the spell Smolyn's veil, later simply known as veil.
* The Netherese arcanist and inventor of many air-related spells Tolodine dies of natural causes aged 57 in his hometown of Imbrue.

* Calim, a djinni lord, arrives in Faerûn together with his entourage of genies and their human and halfling slaves—collectively called the Djen—in the Great Arrival. Calim swiftly claims all lands south-west of the Marching Mountains as the Calim Empire, and bases his rule at Calimport.

Folehar Flametree was a halfling fighter-thief adventurer, merchant, and smuggler based in Elturel in the Western Heartlands in the mid–14 century DR. Circa 1358 DR, he was one of the more important personalities of the city. He traded in rare and special items, including gems stolen from royal treasures, magic looted from tombs, and heirs and heiresses kidnapped from their families, and so on. He was regularly reproached by Lord Dhelt when his smuggling irritated the authorities of Iriaebor, Baldur's Gate, Waterdeep, and Amn.
* An arcanist named Carbury, a master of illusions, poses as the Terraseer in an attempt to gain control of the flying enclave of Spiel. Adventurers unmask Carbury and he is executed for his deceit.
Aaronarra was a copper dragon living on the western side of the High Moor, near the Misty Forest, at the end of the 14th century DR.

Acham el Jhotos, whose full name was Acham yn Aban el Jhotos, yi Almraiven and who was commonly referred to as the Weavepasha, was a mighty wizard and the ruler of Almraiven in Calimshan. He was considered to be one of the most powerful mortals alive in 1479. His entire life was dedicated to defending the city of Almraiven from djinn, efreet, and other menaces. He appeared as an older man but in reality was much older. His oldest granddaughter, the vizar Munaa yr Oma el Jhotos, was nearly 100 years old. Acham was an abolitionist who wanted to free all the slaves in Calimshan.
Forge Fire was an enchanted light hammer that retained the blazing heat of the forge it was crated in.
Abyssal drakes were wild, fiendish creatures related to, and combining the worst traits of, demons, red dragons, and wyverns.

Aerosclughpalar, also called "Gildenfire", Vaeros Fireshield, The Druid Dragon and the Wyrm of Golden Hue, was a neutral gold dragon who, as of 1368 DR, inhabited Tall Trees, in human form, as a druid of Mielikki.
Agatha, also known as the Ghost of Neverwinter Wood, was a banshee who haunted the Neverwinter Wood near Conyberry.
Councilor Florrick was a city official from Baldur's Gate that served the great metropolis of the Sword Coast during the late 15 century DR.
Agatha's Grove was the lair of the banshee Agatha, the "Ghost of Neverwinter Wood".

The Aeltagarr was a sun elf sorceress and seer of the city of Lothen of the Silver Spires in Siluvanede around the 3 century DR. She was known to be kindly and possessing magic enough to rival Magisters, and she was revered as the most senior mage of the realm.
Adrian Martikov was a wereraven vintner who lived and worked at his family's vineyard, the Wizard of Wines, in the domain of Barovia.
Footman's Folly was a unique enchanted shield wielded by distinguished warriors of Neverwinter.
Aconflagblazen was a red dragon who was known as the Steam Snake.

Lord Adreum VI, also remembered as the The Coward Lord of Last, was the last member of the Adreum family of Port Llast who perished in the late 1000s DR and continued to exist as a restless tortured ghost into the late 14 century DR.

Saint Aganna, sometimes known as the lady without fingers, was a saint of the Church of Ilmater famed for treating the sick during the clinging death, a plague which struck Hlondeth in the 1 century DR.
Foestriker was a unique melee weapon wielded by the avatar of Uthgar, the Father of the Uthgardt.
Akkabar Shoon was a mighty wizard, the Pasha of Calimshan and the man ultimately behind the rise of the Shoon Imperium.
Ahmad al-Mudill was a Zakharan flame mage who served as a spy and recruit for the Brotherhood of the True Flame in Zakhara around 1367 DR.
An ahuizotl was a semi-aquatic aberration that mimicked voices and preyed on unwary travelers. It resembled a doglike monkey and had a clawed hand on its tail.
Fortress shield was an enchanted and tall brightly-colored shield once wielded by paladin named Phil Pious before the late 14 century DR.
Albrent was a ghost who haunted the Riverman inn and tavern in Blackfeather Bridge in Featherdale.
Amilektrevitrioelis was an extremely greedy blue hoarder dragon who lived in the Rathgaunt Hills in the Shaar.
An antherion was an animalistic shapechanger that could transform from an animal into a humanoid, or an animal-humanoid hybrid.
The Forgotten Lords was a large and prosperous trading cartel active across the Sword Coast in the late 14 century DR.
Angajuk () was a talking sperm whale that had the ability to speak Common. He was awakened by the druid Anga.
Arnell Hallowleaf was an elven werewolf who devoted himself to the goddess Selûne in the mid-to-late 15 century DR.
Aughiskies, or water-horses (sometimes water horses), were evil, amphibious horses.
Florizan Blank was a famous actor and bard active on the Sword Coast during the late 15 century DR.
Aswidorg was a juvenile black dragon who lived on the High Moor in the Western Heartlands around 1374 DR. Aswidorg was a descendant of the black dragon dracolich Calathanorgoth.

Aubrey Silverspun was a member of the Swords of Leilon, a group of adventurers based in Leilon, in the 14 century DR. After his death, Aubrey's ghost remained in Leilon, running Aubrey's Peculiarities Shoppe in the late 15 century DR.
Augusta Krul was a member of the Swords of Leilon, a group of adventurers based in Leilon in the 14 century DR. After her death, Augusta's ghost remained bound to Leilon until the late 15 century DR.
Force screen was a psionic power of the psychokinesis discipline that granted its user a protective shield of pure force.

Aurgus was a dwarf hero of the Earthspur Mountains in the Vast sometime before the 14 century DR. Aurgus once killed a remorhaz single-handedly in the mountain pass on Mount Aergurl. The local dwarves recalled the event in their lore.
Astalagan was a bronze dragon who was mentioned in the legends about Stormwreck Isle.
Aszhgruzz was a male alguduir, mate of Hizs, one of the two "swamp dragons" who made a home in a swamp and ended lives of several people from a nearby village in the 14 century DR.

The Foundation was a variety of enchanted light flails created on the Sword Coast North in the late 14 century DR, with the original and the most powerful variety once being wielded by the High Inquisitor of Auril.
Baerlatha Luruin was a wizard, potion maker, and animal healer who lived at the Healing House in Bargewright Inn in the Dessarin Valley in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Baen Chalgash was a wererat and a high-ranking member of the Dead Rats gang in Neverwinter.

Azarell was a yochlol who disguised herself as a young elven warrior. She dwelt in the dwarven mines of Icewind Dale in the mid–14 century DR. She may have joined a group of adventurers on their journey to Menzoberranzan.
The Font of Knowledge was a temple of Oghma in Waterdeep on the Sword Coast North in the late 14 century DR. It also included a library, known as the Great Library, and a monastery.
Aziza bint Diyab was an foreign psionicist inhabiting Diyab in Zakhara around 1367 DR.
Awtawmatawn was a unique, larger than average stone golem possessed by a horned devil.
Baba Lysaga was an ancient and powerful hag who lived in Barovia.

Frigid blade is a transmutation spell used by swordmages, particularly those who prefer to use fire and ice together in their spells. When a swordmage casts frigid blade they fill their weapon with icy power, freezing the flesh of its target and the air around it. When used on a creature, this causes the said creature to slow down substantially, the exact percentage dependent upon how durable the swordmage's own flesh is. This effect only lasts a brief moment, though frigid blade can be recast at will and the power of the spell increases with the swordmage's own.
Azamexoc the Pale was a white dragon gladiator and one of the pain-bringers of the Slaughterhouse Arena of Tyraturos at the very end of the 15 century DR.

Baelnorns, sometimes called baelnorn liches, were elves who chose a path of Prime-bound duty beyond death which closely resembled lichdom. They often did so to serve or safeguard their families, communities, or important places, and acted as keepers and protectors of elven clans and holdings far beyond the lifespan of a living elf. As of the turn of the 16 century DR, it was said that some non-elves had discovered a means to become a baelnorn.

Balthazar was a human Bhaalspawn monk and one of the Five who lived in Amkethran in the mid–14 century DR. He was perhaps the most powerful of them, and the only one whose goal was not to achieve power for himself.
Frost was a quality that could be added to a magical weapon, making it dangerously cold.
Baravar Cloakshadow (), known as the Sly One, was the neutral good gnome deity of illusion and deception. His dogma primarily concerned the protection of the gnome race through the art of illusion.

A banshee (), also known as a groaning spirit, or wailing ghost, was a female undead phantom, typically a selfish, strong-willed spirit that embodied the essence of hideousness. Oftentimes they were the spirits of elven women, whom in life had an evil alignment.
Banelar nagas (also simply called banelars) were evil and immortal spell-wielding nagas with large, humanoid heads.
Fual yn Senaor al Barasth was a Calishite sage and a member of the Knights of the Shield in 1370 DR.

Balors ( ), or type VI demons, were the quintessential anarchists of the Abyss, and in some respects the manifestation of the tanar'ric side of the Blood War. Whether acting as generals for demon lord armies or even as minor princelings themselves, balors were warmongering paragons of burning rage that inspired violent defiance against the legions of Hell.

Banderhobbs were enigmatic monsters of shadow and flesh that seemingly hailed from the Shadowfell. They were known for capturing targets at random, by appearing from the shadows as they slept and stealing them away.
Balador, also known as the Lord of Werebears and referred to as Father Bear by his petitioners, was the patron deity of werebears and a protector-god who watched over the forests and woodlands.
Furey was a wizard historian in Luskan and a member of Ship Kurth in the mid–15 century DR.

Bandaerl, son of Rykos, blood of Melair, High Old One of Dumathoin, and protector of Melairbode's essence was a dwarven archlich of the Melairkyn clan who protected the tomb of King Melair I in the depths of Undermountain, formerly home to this ancient clan.
Basilisks () were large, eight-legged reptiles with the terrifying ability to poison or petrify their prey. Though not malicious, basilisks were indisputably dangerous.

Barthus was a vampire priest of Bane who sometime after the Spellplague established himself in the catacombs under the ruins of Spellgard. Using his divine powers, he cowed several undead already there into his service and created more from captured victims.
Fowler was a ship captain that sailed the seas around the Dragon Coast, such as the Dragonmere, during the mid–14 century DR.

The Beast Lord was the local name given to an alhoon mage that dwelled within the ruined mines of Dekanter, carried on horrific arcane experiments, and waged a war against mostly unknown forces of the Underdark, for hundreds of years as of the 15 century DR.
The Lady Bayalun was the step-mother, and later wife, of Yamun Khahan. She was also a talented wizard.

A beholder mage was a beholder which was blind in its central eye—thus lacking its innate antimagic powers—and had taken advantage of this circumstance to train as a wizard. They were one of two kinds of beholders which could cast arcane spells, the other being elder orbs.
Frostsilver armor was distinctive enchanted dwarven armor produced in the hidden forges of Frostsilver Mines prior to that realm's eradication.
Baurthaglos, more commonly known as Anglaspark, was a blue dragon son of the blue wyrm ruler of Turmish, Anaglathos.
Bearpaw was an immensely strong and affable ranger who lived in northwest Faerûn some years before the late 14 century DR.
Bentley Mirrorshade was an industrious gnome illusionist who ran the Friendly Arm Inn.
The frost harpoon was an enchanted spear crafted by the Ulutiun people of the Great Glacier.
Besender Melairkyn was a possessing Clan Melairkyn dwarf ghost in Undermountain in 1375 DR.

Bezelar Mujarif was a well-known psionicist living in Calimshan in the late 1350s DR. He described a tangent of psionic combat as feeling "like a gallstone in the mind" and full contact as "like a tiger has unsheathed its claws in your head".
Beradyx Halfwinter was a human wizard and transportation mage for the Aurora's Realms Shop, Slut Street Catalogue Counter in the Dock Ward of Waterdeep in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
The frostbite blade was a scimitar found in the Storm Horns of Cormyr in the mid-1480s DR.
Besper was a djinni inhabiting the Haunted Lands of Zakhara in .
Bethsheva was the winter wolf bitch and the animal companion of Farghan McFarghan, the herbalist from the village of Hilltop in Luruar in the late 14 century DR.
A bird maiden was a creature unique to the Land of Fate, and was related to the swanmay of Faerûn.
Fured Kiuno of the Bear was a set of enchanted hide armor made from the fur of Chultan moonbear and used by the adventurers of Chult in the late 15 century DR.
Black Shaernauba was a werewyvern brigand reputed to dwell within the Storm Horns mountains in Cormyr in the mid–14 century DR.
Black willows were a sentient and mobile species of tree, akin to a treant, that could alter their forms to look like normal willow trees.

Black Blood hunters were the most vile and depraved lycanthropes among the ranks of the People of the Black Blood, and who had been granted terrible power by their patron god Malar in recognition of their cruelty.

Frostborn armor was a wide variety of enchanted relic light, medium, and heavy armors that included several types of bodywear, headwear, armwear, and footwear, of Ostorian origin, available to adventurers of Neverwinter in the late 15 century DR.
A blink dog was a mysterious, intelligent canine creature. Most blink dogs had yellow-brown fur and large ears. They were well known for their ability to blink—a supernatural teleportation ability.
The Blind was an ancient beholder who lived in Skullport beneath Waterdeep in the 15th century DR.

Blackspawn stalkers were terrifying but nearly mindless predatory dragonspawn combining the worst traits of black dragons and spiders. A related creature was the blackspawn gloomweb, which could also shroud itself in darkness.
Foxleigh was an industrious artisan sculptor active in the late 14 century DR, with his works found in the Western Heartlands, Sword Coast, and the city of Baldur's Gate.

Talontar blightlords, or more commonly just blightlords, were corrupt Talontar priests reveling in decay, feared and reviled throughout the Unapproachable East. They sought to infest its forests with the same blights that had turned the Rawlinswood into a foul mockery of a forest. Most of them served as the Rotting Man's handpicked lieutenants and emissaries, armed with the power to warp forest creatures to their own, sick purposes. Most blightlords had once been clerics, rangers, or even druids. Though some were drawn from other classes, such as the martial or the arcane, all who sought to become a blightlord needed considerable skill at divine magic.
Bladeback was a powerful werewolf bandit who lurked in the King's Forest during the late 15 century DR.
Bluespawn burrowers were large dragonspawn that lived in burrows in the deepest parts of deserts.
Frada's Provisioning was a grocer and ship supplies outfitter on the Rock of Bral in the 14 century DR.
Bluespawn stormlizards were burly, horse-sized dragonspawn that sometimes acted as mounts for other spawn.
Bonebats were a skeletal undead created from the bodies of giant bats or several bat skeletons. Some sages considered them a type of deep bat.
Bonedrinkers were repulsive undead creatures that were created via a certain dark ritual that transformed bugbears into these ghoulish beings and goblins into lesser bonedrinkers.
Fullblades, also known as an ogre's greatsword, were a type of large exotic sword.
Bone golems, sometimes referred to as skeletal golems, were terrifying grisly constructs assembled from bones of various creatures and, despite their appearance, were not undead creatures.
Bonemelt was a powerful enchantment that can transform the solid bones of a mammalian creature into a quivering mass of jelly. The dracolich Daurgothoth was the exclusive caster of this spell.
The Blue Ribbon Pig was an especially large and powerful male swine, the Champion of Pigs, adorned with a blue ribbon with the symbol of Sune's Summer Festival in the late 15 century DR.

The is a four-blade, twin-engine attack helicopter developed by for the United States Army's program to replace the AH-1 Cobra under the designation Model 77. The prototype YAH-64 was first flown on 30 September 1975. The US Army selected the YAH-64 over the in 1976, and later approved full production in 1982. The helicopter was introduced to US Army service in April 1986. It is armed with a 30mm M230 Chain Gun and Hydra rocket pods. __TOC__

Brena Whitebrow was a werewolf cleric of Selûne and one of the leaders of the Fangshields. She was the alpha female and matriarch of the White Pack, and coordinated their efforts with the greater Fangshields organization. She had a son, Brenvol, to whom she taught the responsibilities of leading their pack.
Brainburn was a flameskull member of the Twisted Rune in Undermountain in 1375 DR.
A brain in a jar was the brain of a creature preserved and animated through alchemy and undeath. Liberated of its body, it was capable of great and disturbing psionic powers.

The Steyr AUG (German: Armee-Universal-Gewehr; English: Universal army rifle), also known as the STG.77 (German: Sturmgewehr 77; English: Assault rifle 77), is an Austrian, bullpup-configured assault rifle, designed in the late 1960s by Steyr Mannlicher GmbH & Co KG. The AUG was developed to replace the Austrian army's bulky Stg.58 rifle (a variant of the FN FAL); the AUG fires the lighter 5.56x45mm cartridge, is built from light weight polymers, is compatible with left-handed shooting, and incorporates a built in optical sight. The AUG was adopted by the Austrian army in 1977 and would go on to see large export success with other countries, also being adopted by the militaries of Australia, New Zealand, Oman, Malaysia, and others. The AUG A3 is the most recent version of the AUG, removing the built in sight in favor of a Picatinny rail system to allow mounting of various other optics, foregrips, laser sights, and underbarrel 40mm grenade launchers. The AUG Para is a 9mm SMG variant of the AUG. The AUG A3 appears in six games in the Battlefield series, occasionally named the AUG or STG.77.
Boris was a powerful and sentient magical rapier owned by an adventuring pirate bard in the late 15 century DR.
Bregg, who was nicknamed the Strong, was a renowned Rashemaar berserker who rebelled against the wychlaran.
Borok-Tosst was a ghostly yuan-ti wizard slayer lieutenant who served Nan Kung Chi in the Crypt of Durkon in Kara-Tur in the 14 century DR.
The 40mm Bofors Anti-Aircraft Gun is a flak cannon used for anti-aircraft purposes. It is featured in the Battlefield Series as stationary or unusable emplacements.
Boray Gulditch was an elven kineticist who hunted goblins in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Brian, known as Brian the Swordmaster, was a Masked Lord of Waterdeep in the mid–14 century DR.

Brenvol Whitebrow was a werewolf ranger of Selûne and a member of the Fangshields who served as their liaison to the lycanthropes of Faerûn. He believed that his family, the White Pack served as an example to the evil shapechangers of Toril, proof that faith in the Lady of Silver could keep anyone on the path of good and righteousness.

The 9M133 Kornet (Russian: Корнет) is a Russian anti-tank missile emplacement. It is a second generation ATGM intended to deal with main battle tanks and to engage slow and low flying helicopters, but is not intended to fully replace previous systems, due to the cost. It appears in Battlefield: Bad Company, Battlefield: Bad Company 2, Battlefield Play4Free, Battlefield 3, and Battlefield 4 .

Brondeth of the Broken Staff was a human mage. Alongside Auziiyra Twelvestars and several other mages, Brondeth was guarding a human mining community when they were attacked by drow. The mages used the wonderform spell to hide in the form of wingless wonders and escape being killed, but became lost in the Underdark. They were thought to still be wandering the Night Below by the mid–14 century DR.
Brightfinger was a Netherese arcanist that was known for his development of light-based spells.
A burning man was a type of golem that appeared to be made of scorching coal.

The 2T "Stalker" armored reconnaissance vehicle was developed as a private venture by Belarusian Minotor Service Enterprise with some Russian assistance. The first operational prototype was presented in 2000. This reconnaissance vehicle is intended to operate up to 300 km behind enemy lines and it is used by the MEC in Battlefield: Bad Company, as the faction's only infantry fighting vehicle. __TOC__

Bulezaus () were violence-craving tanar'ri demons that embodied primal fury and the bestial brutality of nature. Though the minotaur-like creatures appeared gaunt, they were the heavy infantry of the Abyss, too stupid and stubborn to retreat. The demonic breed was commonly referred to by planar scholars as "Baphomet's perfect children".
Carbuncles were small armored telepathic animals resembling armadillos with a bright gem in their foreheads.

Camazotz was a chaotic evil lesser deity of bats from the Aztec or Central American pantheon who was worshiped on Toril by the beast cults and on Oerth as part of the Olman pantheon at the city of Tamoachan. On Oerth he was also venerated as a neutral evil lesser deity of vampires and the underworld, under the name Zotzilaha.

The AK-101 is a Russian-made assault rifle designed by Mikhail Kalashnikov in 1994. It is chambered by the 5.56x45mm NATO cartridge, as opposed to the Soviet-made 5.45x39mm cartridge used by most of Kalashnikov's modern designs, and has a rate of fire of 600 rounds per minute with an effective range of 500 meters, and a maximum range of 1000 meters. It is part of the AK-100 series of Assault Rifles.
Chanczlatha Luruin was a cleric of Lathander and a physic and animal healer who lived at the Healing House in Bargewright Inn in the Dessarin Valley in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
Chahir was a vampire sorcerer who resided in the crypts of Dordrien in the Dagger Hills.

The Celestial Emperor, also called the Celestial One and the Master of Heaven, was a deity who ruled the Celestial Empire and oversaw the Celestial Bureaucracy, the dominant pantheon of the continent of Kara-Tur, especially the empire of Shou Lung, and the overarching spiritual state managing its gods, spirits, dragons, and other creatures. Some sages speculated that he was an Overgod.

The AIL Desert Raider is a 6x6 fast attack and surveillance vehicle produced by Automotive Industries Limited of Israel. It is highly regarded as its unique suspension system gives it the mobility of a tracked vehicle, but the stability of a wheeled vehicle. The vehicle is also small enough to be air-dropped from a CH-53. The Raider has been produced since 1998 and is used by the Israeli Defense Force Special Forces as a quick insertion vehicle for teams. Limited numbers have been purchased by the United Kingdom for the SAS and the United States for the Navy SEALs. The Raider has three machinegun mounts that can hold 5.56mm or 7.62mm machine guns.
Ce-ishi was an aging shukenja and healer in the town of Aru in Wa in the 1770s on the Wa Calendar.
Cazador Szarr was an elf vampire lord who lived in Baldur's Gate.
